description: Saskatoon piloted waste diversion methods in public spaces.
Pilots tested sorting, incentives, and reusable foodware.
Results will inform a multi-phase waste diversion plan.

chips.text: Mayor Bulk questioned high contamination rates in public recycling.
Event hosts and public space owners participated in waste pilots.
Public survey identified lack of receptacles, cleanliness, pests as barriers.
Reusable foodware pilot considered cultural needs of Indigenous people.
Project supports 70% waste diversion from city landfill target.
Staff promised a multi-phase waste diversion report in Q2.

description: Saskatoon explores leasing office space on urban reserves.
This could advance reconciliation and Indigenous procurement.
Current leases cost $394,000 annually.

chips.text: Councillor Geller argued for weighing Indigenous treaty rights beyond cost-benefit.
No other city-type municipalities currently pursue urban reserve leases.
No current strategy exists to accommodate all Indigenous employees on urban reserves.
Leasing could provide a vehicle for Indigenous employees to exercise treaty rights.
Administration will continue to assess needs and evaluate urban reserve leasing options.
